PC: Stop sending Susie to bed with the bottle.

Stop bottle propping, a significant choking risk and can lead to ear infections. Remember that Susie’s mother needs support to do her homework. Her mother was receptive to the counseling regarding the appropriate positioning of Susie due to the risk of SIDS, so she may be amenable to removing the bottle due to the choking risk.

Encourage Susie’s mother to start to get Susie accustomed to her mother cleaning her mouth by either wiping the gums daily with a soft, clean washcloth or small, soft toothbrush. This helps set the stage for tooth brushing once the teeth begin to erupt.

Encourage Susie’s mother to seek dental care to have her own teeth repaired. This is to reduce the potential of the inoculation of Susie’s mouth with S. Mutans & other cariogenic bacteria through vertical transmission from her mother to Susie.

Susie’s mom can also chew a Xylitol containing gum. This has been shown to be effective in reducing the vertical transmission of S. Mutans. (Soderling,E. et al, Influence of Maternal Xylitol Consumption on acquisition of Mutans Streptococci by Infants. JDR 79 (3): 882 - 887, 2000) BTW: How much gum would Susie’s mom need to chew daily? Depends on amount of Xylitol in the gum. If it is listed as the first ingredient, probably there is enough Xylitol to be effective. You have to chew in the range of at least 2 pieces, three times a day to have an effect.
